ordered.title: Common questions about engine replacement times

blocks.question: How long does an average engine replacement take in the UK? +
blocks.answer: The average timeline from quote request to completion across all engine types is 5.2 days [EM-VERIFIED]. Reconditioned engines typically take 3-7 days, used engines 3-5 days, and engine rebuilds 2-4 weeks.

blocks.question: What is the fastest engine replacement option? +
blocks.answer: Used engines are typically the fastest, taking 3-5 working days due to UK-wide breaker networks and immediate availability. However, quality and warranty vary significantly. [EM-OBSERVED]

blocks.question: How long does a reconditioned engine take to fit? +
blocks.answer: Reconditioned engine replacement typically takes 3-7 working days from quote to completion. This includes sourcing (1-2 days), delivery (1 day), and installation (1-2 days). [EM-VERIFIED]

blocks.question: Why does an engine rebuild take so long? +
blocks.answer: Rebuilding your own engine takes 2-4 weeks because it involves stripdown (1-3 days), parts ordering (2-7 days), machining work (1-2 weeks), reassembly (3-5 days), and reinstallation (1-2 days). Precision work and specialist machining add significant time. [EM-OBSERVED]

blocks.question: How many labour hours does engine replacement take? +
blocks.answer: Labour hours vary by vehicle type: FWD 8-12 hours , RWD 10-15 hours , 4WD 12-20 hours , and V8/performance 18-24 hours . Professional workshops are significantly faster than DIY (20-40 hours). [EM-OBSERVED]

blocks.question: What factors can delay my engine replacement? +
blocks.answer: Key delay factors include: core exchange availability (in-stock vs built-to-order), vehicle complexity (4WD/V8 take longer), workshop workload (peak season Jan-Mar), unexpected complications (seized bolts, additional worn parts), and parts availability (some OEM components have 12-18 week backorders). [EM-OBSERVED]

blocks.question: Is engine replacement faster at a main dealer or independent? +
blocks.answer: Independents are often faster due to established supply relationships and flexible scheduling. Main dealers may have longer lead times due to OEM parts ordering processes and higher workload. However, main dealers have direct access to OEM parts and technical support. [EM-OBSERVED]

blocks.question: Can I get a courtesy car during engine replacement? +
blocks.answer: Many workshops offer courtesy cars or loan vehicles, but availability varies. Always check when booking. Alternatively, consider hire car coverage as part of your warranty or insurance policy. [EM-OBSERVED]
